# How does Perplexity work?

Perplexity describes its search experience as finding web sources and producing an answer with source links; its Pro Search guide, read on 29 October 2026, explains a deeper search option within that experience. Our construction-software capture on 22 September 2026 named Procore in 21 of 30 Perplexity answers. That observation shows what appeared in our questions, while the provider's documentation explains the reported search feature.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Reported.** The [Perplexity Pro Search guide](https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/10352903-what-is-pro-search), marked modified 26 October 2026 and read on 29 October 2026, describes searching sources, synthesizing information and citing references. It says Pro Search is no longer a separate toggle: Search uses it automatically within the plan's allowance. The guide distinguishes this from other modes; its current feature description is not a label for our earlier capture.

**Measured.** In the [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), ten construction buyer questions supplied three Perplexity runs each. All 30 answers were valid and 21 named Procore. The engine-presence field records naming, not the number of source links and not the quality of the product.

The September count cannot reveal Perplexity's source-selection weights or establish which current search mode produced those earlier answers.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Perplexity responded to “best construction project management software for a mid sized general contractor” on 22 September 2026, run 1, and described Procore with the fragment “project management, financials, field reporting, and subcontractor coordination.” This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read the Search distinction. It describes standard search as a quick answer from a smaller source set and Pro Search as deeper synthesis with more source links. That is Perplexity's explanation of the feature, not a measured difference between modes in our construction panel. The Procore count comes from the retained engine answers, with no mode comparison attached.

For a construction purchase, the Procore cells show why the project context matters. Perplexity named it in all three mid-sized general-contractor answers, but none of the three small residential-builder answers. The 21-of-30 category count combines those contexts. Read the relevant buyer record before treating the total as a shortlist for your job.

The October guide also matters when explaining the interface to a colleague. Instructions to find an old Pro Search toggle would send that reader looking for a control the dated guide says is integrated into Search. State the guide's date and keep that explanation distinct from the September observations.

Procore also had zero names in the three Perplexity answers about an owner managing capital projects. That is an observed omission for a checked vendor, not evidence of a blocked crawler or a product limitation. A question about an owner does different work from the mid-sized contractor question even when both sit in construction software.

# Which construction software does Perplexity recommend?

For a small residential builder, the matching [Perplexity construction question](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) named Buildertrend, Contractor Foreman and JobTread in all three answers, with no Procore match. Procore nevertheless appeared in 21 of 30 across the full category on 22 September 2026. The small-builder cell is included in that total. Read the narrower task before investigating a product; these naming observations do not test what you should buy.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) asked ten construction questions three times on Perplexity, retaining all thirty answers. Procore's 21 of 30 gives 70.0 percent, with a descriptive 95 percent Wilson uncertainty range of 52.1 to 83.3 percent. Capture was 22 September 2026 and publication was 23 September. Thirteen of the 22 checked vendors appeared at least once; all checked labels, including nine zeros, are shown alphabetically.

| Checked vendor | Named in valid Perplexity answers |
| --- | --- |
| Autodesk Construction Cloud | 9 of 30 |
| Buildertrend | 15 of 30 |
| Buildxact | 0 of 30 |
| CMiC | 6 of 30 |
| ConstructionOnline | 2 of 30 |
| Contractor Foreman | 18 of 30 |
| eSUB | 3 of 30 |
| Fieldwire | 12 of 30 |
| Foundation Software | 0 of 30 |
| InEight | 5 of 30 |
| JobTread | 11 of 30 |
| Jonas Construction | 0 of 30 |
| Kahua | 6 of 30 |
| Leap | 0 of 30 |
| Linarc | 0 of 30 |
| Oracle Construction and Engineering | 4 of 30 |
| Penta Software | 0 of 30 |
| Procore | 21 of 30 |
| Raken | 0 of 30 |
| RedTeam | 3 of 30 |
| Sage 300 CRE | 0 of 30 |
| Trimble Viewpoint | 0 of 30 |

The mid-sized-general-contractor question named Procore, Contractor Foreman and JobTread in each of its three Perplexity answers; Buildertrend appeared once. The owner-capital-projects question named Kahua in all three. These are question cells within the same thirty-answer collection. A name match does not reveal whether the answer endorsed the product, which cited publisher supported it or how it would perform on your project.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Perplexity responded to “best construction management software for a small residential builder” on 22 September 2026, run 3, with the fragment “**JobTread**, **Contractor Foreman**, and **Buildertrend**”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Choose the construction role before following a name. A residential builder coordinating jobs, a general contractor managing several parties and an owner overseeing capital projects need different evaluations. Start with the question closest to your work; a larger total can accumulate names from decisions that do not resemble yours.

Write down one operation a candidate must handle and identify the evidence you need to assess it. For estimating or scheduling, that might be a document or demonstration of the specific workflow, with its product edition and conditions recorded. Those are checks for your evaluation. The naming table did not execute the operation or compare delivery outcomes.

Keep the saved wording when tracing an answer's sources. A product can be named without the adjacent capability being supported by the cited passage. Conversely, a publisher may be cited without its own software being offered as an option. This engine table measures names, and it supplies no Perplexity-specific citation rate to substitute for them.

If you publish construction-software information, focus a correction on a demonstrable fact. Retain the answer, the primary source and the disputed statement before revising a page. Verify the served wording after the change and date any later AI observation separately. A zero on the small-builder question is not itself proof of an inaccurate description.
